findings.summary: The dependents list leaves out the tests that read CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md, which this plan changes.
findings.evidence: Grep found refusal_corpus.rs reading CHANGELOG.md with include_str! (for example :1138 and :2986) and decisions.md (:1234, :1771). buy_first.rs reads docs/decisions.md (:105 `unrecorded(Cargo.toml, decisions.md)`, :149 `d36_section`). The plan's entry for D181 and the CHANGELOG entry cites only the append-only rule and names no test. The readers I checked use contains-style lookups, so appending should be safe. Step 9 runs `cargo test --locked`, which would run them. But the list does not name them, so nothing ties them to this change. The real-defaults readers in crates/athena-cap-change/src/lib.rs:143 and :160, crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs:1516, crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs:1795 and crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs:170 are only covered loosely by 'the other defaults.toml readers'. Fix: Add a dependents entry for CHANGELOG.md and decisions.md that names refusal_corpus.rs and buy_first.rs. Give the test to run: `cargo test --locked -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus --test buy_first`. Explain why an append keeps them passing: they check with contains or look up a section by id. Name the cap-change, cap-study, briefs.rs and reading.rs readers of the real defaults.toml, with their crate tests.

findings.summary: Step 1's first sentence still says every pin is changed through repin, which Decision 4 says the text must not claim.
findings.evidence: Step 1 reads: 'version pins, such as `claude_version`, are exact and never auto-floated, and only the person running Athena changes one, through the existing `cargo run -p xtask -- repin` command.' The phrase 'changes one, through … repin' applies to any pin. xtask/src/main.rs:16, :683 and :726-761 show that repin rewrites only `claude_version`. Other pins exist that it cannot move: rust-toolchain.toml:2 `channel = "1.97.0"` and the action SHAs in .github/workflows/ci.yml. This is the same factual slip the earlier attempt was faulted for. Fix: Tie repin to the Claude Code pin inside the first sentence and avoid any '. ' break. For example: 'Version pins are exact and never auto-floated; only the person running Athena moves one, and the Claude Code pin (`claude_version`) moves through the existing `cargo run -p xtask -- repin` command.' Have the new test assert that phrase.

findings.summary: The rule that pins are exact already has tracked exceptions that the plan never mentions.
findings.evidence: pages.yml uses the floating major tags `actions/configure-pages@v5`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3` and `actions/deploy-pages@v4`, while ci.yml pins SHAs. A verifier or a later config job reading the new default would find the repository already breaks it, with no record of whether that is intended. Fix: Have D181 (or a later sentence of the statement) name the floating tags in pages.yml as a known gap and propose a follow-up to pin them to SHAs. pages.yml stays out of scope here, since workflows must not change.

summary: I read the code behind each claim the plan makes, and the claims hold. `DefaultsModel::render` and `first_sentence` are at defaults.rs:58 and :77, and `REPO_DEFAULTS` is at :89. `BudgetSet::Reader => 2_000` is at athena-context/src/lib.rs:176, with the 'never rises' comment at :177-179. The literal `of 2000` is at run_pin_tests.rs:1625. budgets.rs builds the reader set from the real defaults and checks the system-facts line. repin rewrites only `claude_version`, and D180 is the last decision. Production builds the reader prompt from the full `render()` (reading.rs:251), so the new first sentences will reach the reader. The criterion-5 test uses the real file through the production parse and render functions; on the base tree it fails because `get` returns None. My own estimate, not measured: about 445 rendered bytes, about 148 tokens, putting the reader set near 2146, under 2200. The approach is sound. The budget raise was accepted by the user and is recorded as a departure from D170. One finding is major: the dependents list leaves out the tests that read CHANGELOG.md and decisions.md (refusal_corpus.rs and buy_first.rs), and names some real-defaults readers only loosely. Two findings are minor. Step 1's sentence still says every pin moves through repin, which Decision 4 says to avoid. And pages.yml already uses floating action tags, which the new rule does not mention. All three are easy fixes, so the verdict is revise.
